Adaptive mastery: a missed question enters the Incorrect Bank. You can manually remove it at any time, or let it stay there until you answer it correctly 3 times in a row. Adaptive quizzes deliberately pull bank questions more often until they are mastered.

Coverage rule: questions you answer correctly and that are not in the active Incorrect Bank will not recycle until every question in your selected test pool has been shown once. The only exception is an active Incorrect Bank question, which may repeat sooner so you can reach the 3-correct mastery streak.

Regional Anatomy Intro uses its own slide numbers. The other 10 teaching sections reference the Head, Neck, Torso master deck. No supplied slides are marked hidden. Title slides, diagram-only slides without supporting text, and repeated illustrations do not generate standalone questions. Shared content may cite multiple slides.

Intro charts: all bone-count rows, bone-marking definitions, and eligible muscle-name meanings are covered. Examples and Figure columns are excluded. Origin/insertion-only material, including origin-count rows, is excluded.

The instructor file is named Exam 5, but its title slide says Exam 4. Duplicate diaphragm answer-reveal slides are consolidated. Instructor picture questions are retained in the separate self-assessment section.

Slide 4: Identify the occipital triangle of the neck

Original choices: A, B, C, D, E. The instructor answer arrow points to E, but the larger upper posterior triangle is labeled D; E labels the lower subclavian triangle. Confirm the intended key with the instructor.

This list includes levator palpebrae superioris, while the lecture explicitly excludes it from facial-expression muscles (Muscles of mastication slide 18; master slide 58).
